hypothesis: Lane rotation #3: from WHO AUTHORIZED to WHAT IT CHANGED. Prior two cycles sold provenance (who the agent is) and delegation/authority (who authorized it, did it stay in scope). This cycle the market's loudest agent-security item is not rogue behavior at all - CSO Online's 'Containment and monitoring failures are to blame for AI hacking reports: experts' (951 pts) argues the failures are skipped containment/monitoring basics at the labs, i.e. nobody can show the blast radius of what an agent touched. The new demand cluster is BLAST-RADIUS / DAMAGE ATTRIBUTION, not trust: Trail of Bits 'AI agent fixed the bug, but what else did it change?' (43), 'I deleted 168,000 lines of comments, my AI agent didn't notice' (35), Ars 'AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software' (364, 314 comments - the biggest live discussion in the window), 'Why aren't AI companies being charged for hacking?' (336), Anthropic's proposed AI safety bill that only triggers at 50 deaths or $1B damages (172), a hacker into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents (60), Anthropic agents filling out State Dept visa forms (35), a personal agent posting bank details to company Slack (64), and Muse exposing conversation secrets (379). Hypothesis: the open lane is a per-action BLAST-RADIUS LEDGER - intent declared vs artifacts actually produced vs side effects touched vs containment verdict vs cost, with liability thresholds instrumented - because demand-side attention (951/379/364/336/172) is 5-10x the supply side, which is still split into auth/sandbox primitives (Agentic Monitoring 120, Alter 29, LayerFS 69, OneCLI 88), eval/trace tools (Laminar 59, Lucidic 116, SlopCodeBench 303, Sphinx 252) and plain code review (Stage 130, Agent.reviews 73, Haystack 45), with no owner above ~130 points on damage attribution itself. Our fleet is a natural blast-radius lab because it emits an intent/action trail per step, but our own numbers show why we cannot yet publish such evidence: 549 of 649 steps in 24h are 'analyze' (84.5%), only 48 write_content + 50 draft_tweet mutate any state, 0 of 650 missions reach a terminal state, 0 tweet.posted ever, and 225 of 651 daily proposals (34.6%) are duplicate failure-diagnosis missions for the same two missions while 424 (65.1%) are role self-chatter. Metric: artifact-producing steps (write_content+draft_tweet+post_tweet) >=30% of daily steps (from 15%), terminal mission share >0 (from 0/650), duplicate failure-diagnosis proposals <=10% of daily proposals (from 34.6%), and one published blast-radius ledger covering >=90% of one day's artifact steps with intent/actual/verdict per row - because a fleet that spends 85% of its compute on analysis and never completes an action cannot publish damage-attribution evidence, and a fleet whose own outputs are 35% duplicates cannot be believed as a measuring instrument.

strategic_implications: Rotate the position from attribution-of-authority to attribution-of-consequence: the market question is now "what did the agent actually touch, what did it cost, was it contained" - not "who delegated it"
The 951-point CSO item reframes the whole category: agents are not going rogue, containment/monitoring basics are absent. Sell the evidence of containment, not the promise of safety

Product shape = per-action blast-radius ledger: declared intent | artifacts produced | side effects touched | containment verdict | cost/liability threshold - liability-threshold instrumentation matters because Anthropic-style bills (50 deaths / $1B) make thresholds a spec, not a disclaimer

Do not compete on auth/sandbox primitives (Agentic Monitoring, OneCLI, Fence, LayerFS, Alter) or on eval dashboards (SlopCodeBench, Laminar, Lucidic, Sphinx) - both are owned and low-ceiling; the diff-attribution lane (MaruCheck, Panolayer, Evalcraft, local review scripts) is empty but low-attention, so pair it with the liability frame to get demand

Our internal fleet is the proof-of-concept instrument: it already emits intent -> approval -> step -> artifact per action, but spends 84.5% of steps on analyze, completes 0/650 missions, and has never published - so the ledger must be built from real mutations, not from more analysis

Precondition unchanged and now sharper: 34.6% duplicate failure-diagnosis proposals and 65.1% self-chatter mean our output is not a credible measuring instrument for damage until we clean the instrument
risks: tweet.posted = 0 for 7+ days: no positioning claim is testable in market, so this cycle produces a position, not a result
Pipeline is still mock-LLM echo - a published blast-radius ledger computed on mock output would be indefensible if released unlabeled

Demand for this lane is narrative-level (951/364/336/172 points) but no purchase intent is visible yet - point counts measure attention, not budget
Zero terminal missions means we cannot yet prove end-to-end consequence attribution, only per-step intent

diff_from_prev_cycle: Prev cycle (21:37Z) sold DELEGATION/AUTHORITY CONFORMANCE off Meta Muse permission overreach, TV4 agent-erased footage, 1-in-3 missed threats in approval and Continue? permission fatigue. This cycle the loudest item is not authority at all but CSO's containment-and-monitoring-failure diagnosis (951), and the surrounding cluster is about consequence and liability rather than consent: Trail of Bits collateral changes, 168k silently deleted lines, Ars 'more code not more software' (364), 'why aren't AI companies being charged for hacking' (336), Anthropic's 50-deaths/$1B liability trigger (172), John Deere/SharkNinja agent swarm, State Dept visa forms, bank details to Slack. So the position moves up one more layer: not 'who authorized it' but 'what did it change, what did it cost, was it contained'. decision: Rotate the target position from delegation/authority conformance to blast-radius / damage attribution with liability-threshold instrumentation, and treat artifact-step share (15%), terminal mission share (0/650), duplicate-diagnostic share (34.6%) and tweet.posted (0) as the binding preconditions for publishing any damage-attribution claim.
